title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: S is a normal base scheme (in the 'arithmetic case', of finite type over Q). U_S over S is a relative curve, the complement in a smooth proper curve X_S of an étale divisor T of cusps. K is the function field of S and E_K = Gal(K̄/K), or the arithmetic fundamental group over the generic point. The aim is to show that a section of the extension of fundamental groups that comes from a K-point and is 'unramified' over S actually comes from an S-point of U_S. In other words, a K-point (or a point over an open S' ⊂ S) extends over S when its section of π_1 extends over E_S.

Step 1, genus 0 (end of the previous argument). Take one of the sections of the cusp divisor T over S as the section at infinity. After localizing on S, one may assume U_S = E^1_S \ T', where E^1_S is the affine line, i.e. P^1_S minus the infinity section, and T' is the remaining cusps. A point f defined over S' = S \ Z is then a section of the affine line over S', i.e. an element of Γ(S', O_S). Since codim(Z,S) ≥ 2 and S is normal, Hartogs/S2 extension makes f extend to a global function, i.e. a section of E^1_S over S. Avoiding T' is then handled 'as before': on the previous pages, via the extensions (13) and the obstruction ξ_i, using the uniformizer along a cusp section.

Step 2, start of the codimension-one analysis.
- Let D_i be the irreducible divisors of S, equivalently the codimension-1 points x_i, whose local rings O_{x_i} are DVRs because S is normal.
- Take the integral closure of O_{x_i} in K̄ and choose a maximal ideal x̃_i over x_i. These correspond to the points over x of the normalization S̃ of S in K̄.
- Let N_x̃ be the stabilizer of x̃ in E_K, the decomposition group. It acts on k(x̃) = k(x)‾ and maps onto Gal(k(x)‾/k(x)) (standard decomposition-group surjectivity).

The next page continues the same argument:
- the inertia group I_x̃ is the kernel of this map, giving 1 → I → N → Gal(k(x)‾/k(x)) → 1;
- in characteristic 0, Kummer theory gives I ≅ Ẑ(1) = T_∞(K̄*);
- by purity on a normal base, ker(E_K → E_S) is the normal subgroup generated by the I_x̃;
- so splitting over this kernel reduces to splitting over each inertia group, i.e. to a DVR-by-DVR analysis.

This is the standard 'good reduction / unramified section ⇒ point extends' argument: reduce to DVRs in codimension 1, then extend over codimension ≥ 2 by Hartogs.
errors: Gap: the extended section f of E^1_S must also be shown to avoid the cusps T' over all of S, not only over S'. The page defers this to 'comme précédemment' and does not give it on this page.
Notation slip: the codimension-1 points are written 'pts x_i de X' though the divisors D_i live on S; presumably points of S, or of the base of X.
The DVR property of O_{x_i} uses the normality of S, which is assumed but not repeated at this point.
Hartogs extension needs S normal (or S2) and Z of codimension ≥ 2; both are stated, so the step is fine.

ideas.what: Extension of a point of the affine line over the complement of a codimension ≥ 2 closed subset of a normal base (Hartogs/S2 extension), used for the genus-0 case after taking a cusp as the infinity section.
Decomposition and inertia groups at codimension-1 points of a normal base, with the exact sequence 1→I→N→Gal(k(x)‾/k(x))→1 and I ≅ Ẑ(1) in characteristic 0.
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition/inertia groups of divisorial valuations; tame inertia ≅ Ẑ(1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hilbert, classical ramification theory; SGA 1 for the scheme version

ideas.what: Reducing 'a section of π_1 over the generic point extends over S, hence the point extends over S' to splitting over each divisorial inertia group, then extending over codimension ≥ 2.
ideas.modern_name: Unramified sections and good reduction / specialization of sections over higher-dimensional bases
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings (section conjecture over finitely generated fields); later worked out by Stix and others
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) states the conjecture for finitely generated bases; this detailed reduction is not, to my knowledge, in his published texts

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a standard reduction: Hartogs extension in codimension ≥ 2, and decomposition/inertia groups at divisors with purity. It serves to extend points with unramified sections over a normal base. This is consistent with Grothendieck's known view of the section conjecture over finitely generated bases, and the techniques are classical and appear in later work (e.g. Stix's book). It is interesting as a draft but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'E'_S' is most likely E^1_S, the affine line over S, matching the later '$\mathbb{E}^1_S$'.
'd'image [?] en fait, on le sait, sur Gal(...)' should read 's'envoie en fait, on le sait, sur Gal(k(x)‾/k(x))'.
'son [?] stabilisateur N_x dans son [?] E_K': the second 'son' is likely just 'dans', i.e. 'son stabilisateur N_x dans E_K'.
'anneau jong [?]' is unclear in the image; it is glossed in the parentheses as 'anneau de valuation discrète'.
